findings.title: Initial seek failure reports activation success and retains the acquired run

steps: Have the isolated scene stub successfully return a run, then throw CHANGED_NATIVE_BINDING from its first apply(0).
Await preview.activate(); inspect return value, phase, error and dispose counters.

findings.observed: activate() returns true while snapshot.phase is error. The acquired run has zero dispose calls and its source reader remains undisposed until explicit stop. seek() catches the exception and returns false, so activate() does not enter its cleanup catch.
findings.expected: A failed first frame must make activation fail and release the newly acquired controller/reader; activation success must match a ready initialized preview.
findings.why_it_matters: The UI/controller join treats failed initialization as successful and retains ownership that can block subsequent native/legacy actions until manual close. This probe establishes wrapper behavior under a controller refusal, not that current accepted assets actually trigger that refusal.
findings.confidence: high for component control flow; actual accepted-scene trigger not executed

findings.title: Stop erases the saved failure contrary to required error retention

steps: Trigger a controller apply refusal in the isolated component.
Invoke reset: the existing error remains.
Invoke stop: inspect snapshot.error and status.

findings.observed: CHANGED_NATIVE_BINDING survives reset but stop changes error to null, phase to idle and replaces the failure status with a restoration message. Legacy selector capture handlers also call this stop path.
findings.expected: Stop/reset should restore or pause the preview while retaining the last error for diagnosis, as specified in this audit brief.
findings.why_it_matters: Closing or switching away removes the evidence of the refusal, so callers/UI cannot distinguish a failed preview from a cleanly stopped preview.

findings.title: Public stop resurrects a disposed component and permits detached reactivation

steps: Call dispose(), then stop(), then await activate() while the supplied scene remains live.

findings.observed: dispose sets phase disposed and removes the panel; stop unconditionally changes phase back to idle. activate then succeeds, acquires another run and reports ready on a removed panel whose general event controller is already aborted.
findings.expected: Disposed must be terminal; stop should preserve disposed and activation must remain refused after disposal.
findings.why_it_matters: A retained controller reference can reacquire scene ownership without a usable panel/close button. Current warehousePage clears its component reference on teardown, which narrows production reachability; this is a component API lifecycle defect.
findings.confidence: high for component API; low production reachability in current page ownership
